answer.summary: Liu cautions established companies not to treat AI as a marketing add-on or a handful of features. Instead, they should reassess from a clean slate how to pursue their mission as an AI-native company, then honestly decide whether their existing assets help or hinder that approach.

sections.heading: The mistake to avoid
sections.content: Don’t just add “some AI stuff” to the marketing site and a couple of AI features, then call the adaptation done. Liu says companies that predate GenAI need to take a clean-slate look at how their mission would be carried out if they were founding the company today with a fully AI-native approach.

sections.heading: Assess the legacy business honestly
sections.content: After rethinking the mission, determine whether the existing product and business provide useful building blocks or whether the legacy assets leave the company worse off than starting from scratch. Liu says the answer depends on the product; if the company cannot conclude that its existing pieces make it better positioned, he advises finding a buyer and, if still committed to the mission, starting its next incarnation. He says Airtable’s no-code components were useful building blocks for its own mission.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately identifies Liu’s warning against adding a few AI features or marketing changes and calling the adaptation complete. It also grounds the clean-slate, AI-native reassessment and legacy-assets discussion in S1 and S2.
